extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (and patent practitioners preparing/responding to Office actions)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining when a claim limitation is to be interpreted under 35 U.S.C. 112(f) (pre‑AIA 112 sixth paragraph), how to apply the three‑prong test, the resulting scope (corresponding structure/equivalents), presumptions from use/absence of “means/step,” and drafting/response options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadest reasonable interpretation (BRI)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims in this application are given their broadest reasonable interpretation using the plain meaning of the claim language in light of the specification as it would be understood by one of ordinary skill in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plain meaning in light of the specification when construing claims. See slide references in the source. BRI is the starting point for claim interpretation during examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification limits BRI when 35 U.S.C. 112(f) applies
rubrics_metrics.description: The broadest reasonable interpretation of a claim element (also commonly referred to as a claim limitation) is limited by the description in the specification when 35 U.S.C. 112(f) or pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph, is invoked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a limitation is interpreted under 112(f), the claim element is not given unconstrained BRI but is limited to the corresponding structure/material/acts described in the specification (and equivalents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Three‑prong test for 112(f) interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: As explained in MPEP 2181, subsection I, claim limitations that meet the following three‑prong test will be interpreted under 35 U.S.C. 112(f) or pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (A) the claim limitation uses the term “means” or “step” or a term used as a substitute for “means” that is a generic placeholder (nonce or non‑structural term) for performing the claimed function; (B) the term is modified by functional language (typically linked by “for”, e.g., “means for”, or phrases like “configured to” or “so that”); and (C) the term is not modified by sufficient structure, material, or acts for performing the claimed function. If all three prongs are met, interpret under 112(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption from use of 'means' or 'step'
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of the word “means” (or “step”) in a claim with functional language creates a rebuttable presumption that the claim limitation is to be treated in accordance with 35 U.S.C. 112(f) or pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presumption can be rebutted when the claim limitation recites sufficient structure, material, or acts to entirely perform the recited function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption from absence of 'means' or 'step'
rubrics_metrics.description: Absence of the word “means” (or “step”) in a claim creates a rebuttable presumption that the claim limitation is not to be treated in accordance with 35 U.S.C. 112(f) or pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: That presumption is rebuttable when the claim limitation recites function without reciting sufficient structure, material, or acts to entirely perform the recited function (i.e., a generic placeholder coupled with functional language can still trigger 112(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of interpreting a limitation under 112(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because this/these claim limitation(s) is/are being interpreted under 35 U.S.C. 112(f) or pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph, it/they is/are being interpreted to cover the corresponding structure described in the specification as performing the claimed function, and equivalents thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When 112(f) applies, the claim is limited to the corresponding structure/material/acts disclosed in the specification (and their equivalents) — examiners should state the identified corresponding structure in the Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and grouping of multiple §112(f) limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple §112(f) limitations need explanation, they can be handled in a single paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use FP 7.30.06 to list multiple limitations (e.g., “Such claim limitation(s) is/are: a device for cutting in claim 4; a mechanism for rotating the device around the fork in claim 4.”). Examiners may format insertions as a list or chart and may provide a single explanation regarding repeated use of certain generic placeholders. Dependent claims can be added when using FP 7.30.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph use and when a heading is needed
rubrics_metrics.description: This heading only needs to be used when the action includes remarks regarding claim interpretation. If Hypothetical claim 1 was the only claim under examination, there would be no need to use this heading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the claim interpretation heading and the appropriate FP (e.g., FP 7.30.03, FP 7.30.05, FP 7.30.06, FP 7.30.07) when the Office action includes substantive remarks on claim interpretation; otherwise omit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant options to avoid or change 112(f) interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant does not intend to have this/these limitation(s) interpreted under 35 U.S.C. 112(f) or pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph, applicant may: (1) amend the claim limitation(s) to avoid it/them being interpreted under 35 U.S.C. 112(f) (e.g., by reciting sufficient structure to perform the claimed function); or (2) present a sufficient showing that the claim limitation(s) recite(s) sufficient structure to perform the claimed function so as to avoid it/them being interpreted under 35 U.S.C. 112(f) or pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advise applicants of the two remediation paths: amendment to add structure, or evidentiary/argument showing that sufficient structure already exists in the claim/specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Means' reciting sufficient structure is not treated under 112(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: This application includes one or more claim limitations that use the word “means” or “step” but are nonetheless not being interpreted under 35 U.S.C. 112(f) or pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph because the claim limitation(s) recite(s) sufficient structure, materials, or acts to entirely perform the recited function. Such claim limitation(s) is/are: a knife blade means for cutting in claim 6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because these limitations are not being interpreted under 112(f), they are not being interpreted to cover only the corresponding structure/material/acts described in the specification and equivalents. If applicant intends 112(f) treatment, applicant may amend to remove the structure or present a showing that the recited structure is insufficient.
